explanation: Mark Antony speaks it at Caesar's funeral. He claims he has come to bury Caesar, not to praise him, then turns the crowd against Brutus and the other conspirators.

claims.text: In Julius Caesar, Mark Antony says 'Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears'.
The line does not come from Antony and Cleopatra, Coriolanus or Hamlet.
Antony speaks the line in his funeral speech for Caesar, saying he has come to bury Caesar, not to praise him.
Antony's speech turns the Roman crowd against Brutus and the other conspirators.
